subject: Recenter GPU pools for Q3 pilot + autoscale carveout
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recenter GPU pools for Q3 pilot + autoscale carveout

Team —

Quick context: Orion Labs is greenlighting a production pilot for their real-time inferencing workflow (low-latency, bursty daytime traffic). They asked for a small, isolated slice of Dedicated capacity for 90 days to ensure SLOs while we iron out autoscale behavior. I ran a light analysis and proposed a "pool recentering" to create a 25% headroom buffer for low-latency pilots by shifting ephemeral capacity away from least-utilized background pools.

What I'm asking for here:
- Ops/Capacity: can we create a temporary carveout of ~12 RTX A10G-equivalent slots (approx 240 A100-equivalent tokens/min baseline) in us-west for 90 days starting 2027-04-01?
- Policy/Product: an exception to the default autoscale preemption policy so the carveout won't be immediately reclaimed during autoscaling churn (we'd still accept soft-preemption after a 72-hr notice).
- Finance/Procurement: accept the provisional billing quote from CloudX while we finalize terms with Orion (attached).

I attached a short plan (pool_recenter_plan_v1.xlsx) and the pilot scope doc (pilot_scope.md). Highlights:
- Measured median CPU/GPU utilization on candidate pools: 38% (batch-heavy) vs 67% (low-latency).
- Proposed movement: reassign 16 ephemeral GPUs from background batch pool -> create 12-slot pilot slice + 4-slot safety buffer.
- Expected impact: ~6% increase in tail latency for some batch jobs during busy windows unless we throttle them by policy flag.

Timeline proposal: decision by 2027-03-10, carveout created 2027-04-01, pilot ends 2027-06-30.

Next steps I suggest: ops review capacity feasibility, product to confirm rollback/fallback criteria, procurement to review billing attachment.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- pool_recenter_plan_v1.xlsx (XLSX)
- pilot_scope.md (MD)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recenter GPU pools for Q3 pilot + autoscale carveout

Thanks Karthik — useful framing. A couple quick clarifying questions before Ops commits: 

1) Can you confirm the expected steady-state utilization for the carveout (p50/p95)? The spreadsheet lists a range but I'd like a succinct number for SLO planning.
2) What are the exact preemption guarantees you want? "Soft-preemption after 72h notice" is reasonable, but Product should specify whether we allow emergency preemption for safety/security incidents.
3) Will Orion require dedicated tenancy/networking (Private) or is this standard Dedicated (shared control plane)?

Marcus/Tessa, can you do a fast feasibility check on:
- mapping 12 A10G-equivalent -> concrete slot types we have in us-west (list preferred);
- whether rebalancing those 16 ephemeral GPUs triggers any autoscale flapping rules or long tail eviction cascades?

I'll loop Legal/Finance once Marcus confirms the slot mapping. If this lands cleanly we can approve a provisional carveout with a policy stub in the Console (pilot:orion-2027).

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Mar 2027 09:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recenter GPU pools for Q3 pilot + autoscale carveout

Kimberly/Karthik — quick take from capacity side after a 30-min triage with infra: 

- Slot mapping: we have two candidate flavors in us-west that are straightforward: 12 x A10G slots (preferred) or 8 x A100-small + 4 x A10G (mixed) if we need to reduce contiguous allocation. I'll attach a short mapping table to the shared doc.
- Utilization expectation: p50 ~ 45% GPU, p95 ~ 78% under peak synthetic traffic (Karthik's load profile). That gives ~20% headroom for sudden spikes; we should keep the 4-slot safety buffer.
- Autscale/policy risk: moving capacity will temporarily increase queueing on the batch pool for ~24-48 hours; however, we can mitigate with scheduled throttles and by enabling prefix caching on the busiest models. No cascading evictions expected if we hold soft-preemption for 72h.

Operational ask: we need sign-off on the exception policy text so we can add it to the carveout request in the Console. Proposed text: 
"Pilot carveouts are carved from ephemeral pools and are exempt from immediate autoscale preemption for a 90-day pilot window; emergency preemption remains permitted for security or hardware-critical incidents with 24-hour notice.

If everyone is aligned I'll schedule the capacity move for the 2027-04-01 maintenance window and send the Console request.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Capacity Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Evan Cho <evan@orionlabs.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Mar 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recenter GPU pools for Q3 pilot + autoscale carveout

Karthik/Kimberly — really appreciate the quick turnaround. From Orion's side:
- We confirm we do NOT need Private (VPC) for the initial 90-day pilot; Dedicated with isolated slot reservation is fine.
- SLO ask: 99th percentile token latency <= 420ms during weekdays 09:00-18:00 PT. Is the p95/p99 profile Marcus quoted expected to meet that with the proposed carveout?
- Billing: CloudX provided a provisional quote (cc'd cloudx-billing@cloudx.com). We can accept provisional billing to get started but will want a simple cap and credit if preemption occurs.

If you can confirm latency and the soft-preemption terms, we'll sign the pilot MOU and confirm start date.

Evan
Evan Cho
Head of ML Platform, Orion Labs

On Wed, Mar 9, 2027 at 09:45 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com> wrote:
> Evan — thanks, that's helpful. Marcus says p95/p99 mapping looks plausible but we'll run a short synthetic baseline next week to validate 99th token latency.
> 
> -Kimberly

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Evan Cho <evan@orionlabs.com>, cloudx-billing@cloudx.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recenter GPU pools for Q3 pilot + autoscale carveout

Thanks everyone — short summary and asks: 

1) Agreement: Ops confirms mapping and risk posture; Product approves the 72h soft-preemption exception with emergency 24h preemption carve-out.
2) Orion: confirm MOU and cap language; Marcus will run a 2-hour synthetic test next Tue (2027-03-16 10:00 PT) to validate p99 latency.
3) Finance: accept provisional CloudX billing with a one-time credit clause if preemption occurs (Finance to draft).

I uploaded the updated plan to the shared docs (link in metadata) and attached the CloudX quote for Finance review. If no objections by EOD 2027-03-11 I'll file the carveout request and schedule the maintenance move 2027-04-01.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
